beginner.summary: For developers who write Python or C# and are new to Semantic Kernel. Covers installing the SDK, connecting to Azure OpenAI with keys and Entra ID, the kernel and service registry, chat history, execution settings, streaming, native and prompt functions, plugins, automatic function calling and tool choice modes, structured output, prompt files, error handling, logging and offline testing, finishing with an IT helpdesk assistant capstone.
prerequisites: Writes working programs in Python 3 or C# with async and await
Uses a terminal, Git and a package manager such as pip or dotnet
Has an Azure subscription or lab access with an Azure OpenAI chat deployment and rights to read its endpoint
outcomes: Connect the kernel to Azure OpenAI using keys or Microsoft Entra ID and run chat completions
Expose application code as plugins and let a model call it through automatic function calling
Write prompt functions and templates and request structured output
Test, log and troubleshoot a kernel application without relying on a live model
